name: Physician
description: ⚠⚠⚠ There is no pre-medical major, and AAMC's own numbers say the medical-sounding one is the worst choice. Of 54,699 applicants in 2025-26, 58.6% majored in biological sciences and were admitted at 42.1% against an overall 42.9% — while mathematics and statistics reached 57.3%, humanities 52.0% and physical sciences 51.3%. ⚠⚠ Specialized health sciences came LAST at 40.3%. Six Florida public medical schools award 757 degrees a year.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ FLORIDA CHANGED THE ROUTE IN 2024, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST LICENSURE CHANGE ON THIS SITE. CS/SB 7016, signed 21 March 2024 as chapter 2024-15, EXEMPTS qualifying internationally trained physicians from the United States residency requirement. Under s. 458.311(8)(e) an applicant may be certified without an approved residency if they hold an active unencumbered licence to practise medicine in a foreign country, have actively practised medicine during the ENTIRE FOUR-YEAR PERIOD preceding the application, completed a residency or substantially similar postgraduate training recognised in their licensing jurisdiction, hold an active valid ECFMG certificate, and ⚠⚠ have AN OFFER FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYMENT as a physician from a health care provider operating in Florida. An applicant who does not qualify for unrestricted licensure may be certified on a restricted basis instead, and must notify the Board of Medicine of any change of employment. ⚠ The same act repealed the old s. 458.3124 restricted-licence provision, enacted the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact in Florida, and created the TEACH Funding Program for clinical training. ⚠⚠⚠ Read what that means about the supply problem: faced with a physician shortage, Florida's answer was partly to admit doctors who trained somewhere else, tied to a job offer — not only to build more pipeline. ⚠ For a domestically trained applicant nothing changed: an accredited medical school, USMLE or COMLEX, and a residency, which remains the real bottleneck.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The major does not matter, and the one that sounds like it does is last

AAMC Table A-17, academic year 2025-26. Acceptance rates computed from the published applicant and matriculant counts:

Primary undergraduate majorApplicantsMatriculantsRateApplicant mean MCAT
✅ Mathematics and statistics33519257.3%511.6
✅ Humanities1,45375552.0%508.8
✅ Physical sciences4,2432,17551.3%509.6
Social sciences4,7582,01442.3%505.8
⚠ Biological sciences⚠⚠ 32,03813,480⚠ 42.1%506.3
Other9,2883,78340.7%505.3
⚠⚠⚠ Specialized health sciences2,5841,041⚠⚠ 40.3%⚠ 504.0 — lowest
All applicants54,69923,44042.9%506.3

⚠⚠⚠ Biological sciences is 58.6% of the entire applicant pool and is admitted at below the overall rate. Specialized health sciences — the most medicine-sounding category in the table — is last on both rate and MCAT.

⚠⚠ Now the caution, because it changes what you may conclude

These are selection effects, not causes. Mathematics and statistics is 335 people, self-selected and unusual. Nobody becomes a better candidate by switching major.

⚠⚠⚠ And look at the matriculant column, which is where the real point is: the scores CONVERGE. Admitted students average 511.9 from biological sciences, 513.0 from humanities, 515.8 from mathematics, 512.1 overall. The bar is the same everywhere. What differs is who clears it.

⚠ So the honest claim is narrow, and it is the same one this site's Lawyer path reached from LSAC data: the evidence gives no support to choosing a major BECAUSE its title sounds like the profession. Study what you are good at, clear the prerequisite coursework, and take the MCAT seriously.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida's 2024 answer to its physician shortage: import doctors

CS/SB 7016, signed on 21 March 2024, exempts qualifying internationally trained physicians from the US residency requirement. Under s. 458.311(8)(e) the applicant must:

  • hold an active, unencumbered licence to practise medicine in a foreign country;
  • have actively practised medicine during the entire four-year period preceding the application;
  • have completed a residency or substantially similar postgraduate training recognised in that jurisdiction;
  • hold an active valid ECFMG certificate; and
  • ⚠⚠ hold an offer of full-time employment as a physician from a health care provider operating in Florida.

⚠⚠⚠ That last condition is the whole design: the licence follows the job. The same act repealed the older restricted-licence provision, enacted the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact and created the TEACH Funding Program for clinical training.

⚠ For a Florida student nothing changed — medical school, USMLE or COMLEX, residency. But it tells you something worth knowing before committing twelve years: the state's fastest lever on its own shortage was not more medical school seats.

⚠⚠ Primary care is growing through nurse practitioners, not physicians

Role2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2024–34
Family medicine physician$244,180116,000⚠ 3,300⚠ average (3–4%)
Nurse practitioner$132,300320,400✅ 29,500✅ much faster (7%+)
Physician assistant$135,880162,70012,000✅ much faster (7%+)

⚠⚠⚠ Nine times as many nurse practitioner openings a year as family medicine physician openings. Family medicine pays roughly $110,000 more and is growing at average rates while both advanced-practice routes grow much faster. That is the structure of American primary care, and it should be part of a decision that costs twelve years.

⚠⚠ The anaesthesia comparison, which surprises almost everyone

AnesthesiologistNurse anesthetist
2025 median$391,490$236,590
Employed45,300⚠⚠ 53,800
Openings a year1,300⚠⚠ 2,700
Routemedical school + 4-year residencyRN licence + doctorate

⚠⚠⚠ The nursing occupation is LARGER than the physician one it works beside, and has twice the annual openings. The physician earns $154,900 more. Both facts are true and a student should weigh both.

⚠ Six schools, 757 degrees

InstitutionMD credentials (2023)

Florida International University118

⚠ These are the PUBLIC schools. This site does not list private or osteopathic institutions, and Florida has several, so 757 is the public-tuition output rather than the state's total.

✅ The prerequisites are cheap and local — with one exception

Every standard prerequisite is carried widely across Florida's public colleges: composition and calculus at 39 institutions, statistics at 39, psychology at 33, organic chemistry I and II at 29 each, sociology at 29, calculus-based physics at 25, general biology at 20, general chemistry at 15.

⚠⚠⚠ The exception is BCH3023 Biochemistry: SEVEN carriers, and upper division. It is the one prerequisite likely to force a transfer or an online course, and it is also tested on the MCAT. Plan for it in your first year, not your third.

Necessary skills

  • Sustained, unglamorous memorisation for two years, followed by sustained decision-making under uncertainty for the rest of your life.
  • Comfort being wrong in public and correcting fast. Diagnosis is iterative and the first answer is often not the answer.
  • Physical and emotional endurance. Residency is three to seven years of it, and it comes after the four.
  • Reading the literature critically — which is one reason the statistics and physical sciences majors do well on the way in.
  • Talking to frightened people in plain words, which is the skill the humanities majors bring and the one patients notice.
  • Tolerance for a twelve-year plan in which the money arrives at the end and the debt arrives at the start.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Major in something you will get high grades in and enjoy. The prerequisites are courses, not a degree, and the data says the biology-by-default choice performs slightly below average. This is the most useful and most ignored advice on this page.

⚠⚠ Find biochemistry early. Seven Florida public institutions carry it and it is upper division. Everything else you can take at a state college near home.

⚠ Look honestly at PA and nurse practitioner before committing. Not because medicine is not worth it, but because the primary-care numbers above are what the job market is actually doing, and the training differential is eight years.

⚠ Treat residency as the real bottleneck — medical school admission is the famous hurdle and the match is the one that decides your specialty, your income and where you live.

And read s. 458.311(8)(e) if you trained abroad. Florida will license you without a US residency if you have four unbroken years of practice, ECFMG certification and a Florida job offer. That is a genuinely unusual provision and it took effect in March 2024.

programs.note: The MD programme — 6 Florida public institutions, 757 credentials, 749 professional doctorates. USF 179, UF 149, FSU 125, UCF 122, FIU 118, FAU 64. ⚠ Read its degrees note for the AAMC acceptance-rate table and the biochemistry problem.

⚠⚠ The comparison worth making on structure rather than prestige: two to three years against four plus a three-to-seven-year residency, and a PA can change specialty without retraining. ⚠ Six Florida public programmes each — the same count, very different lengths, and the PA route needs ~3,200 patient care hours before applying where medicine does not.

⚠⚠⚠ Named for the anaesthesia comparison: 53,800 nurse anesthetists against 45,300 anesthesiologists, and 2,700 annual openings against 1,300. ⚠ The nursing occupation is larger than the physician one beside it, at $236,590 against $391,490 — and it is reached through an RN licence and a doctorate rather than medical school and a four-year residency.
⚠ The MD/MPH is a common pairing and public health is where much physician policy, epidemiology and population work happens. 8 Florida institutions, all universities, 579 master's a year.

⚠ An honest alternative rather than a route: the same chemistry and biology prerequisites, a licensed Florida profession, $82,280 on a bachelor's, and four years instead of twelve. ⚠⚠ Named because a student who loves the science but not the decade should see it before committing.

⚠ Not a route in, but the commonest route out of full-time clinical practice — physician executives sit inside the medical and health services manager occupation. Named so a twelve-year plan is made with its exits visible.

courses.reason: General Biology I — 20 institutions. The majors-level sequence every medical school prerequisite list names, and the foundation for the MCAT's biological sciences section.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Not interchangeable with BSC2085 Anatomy and Physiology. Medical schools want the majors biology sequence; the A&P sequence is the nursing and allied-health one.

courses.reason: General Biology II — 18 institutions. The second half, usually ecology, evolution and organismal biology.
General Chemistry I — 15 institutions. Universally required and the gate to organic chemistry.
General Chemistry II — 15 institutions. Required everywhere, and a common place where pre-medical plans quietly end.
Organic Chemistry I — 29 institutions. Required by essentially every medical school and heavily represented on the MCAT.
Organic Chemistry II — 29 institutions. The second half; some schools accept biochemistry in its place, most do not.

⚠⚠⚠ Biochemistry — only SEVEN Florida public institutions carry it, and it is upper division. It is a near-universal prerequisite and a major MCAT topic, which makes it the single hardest prerequisite to obtain locally.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Plan for this in your first year. With seven carriers it is the prerequisite most likely to force a transfer, a summer elsewhere or an online course — and doing it late leaves you unprepared for the MCAT as well as short a requirement.

courses.reason: Physics with Calculus I — 25 institutions. Required by most medical schools, and the calculus-based version is the safer choice if you might apply to engineering-adjacent or research programmes too.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida also carries algebra-based PHY2053 at 19 institutions and PHY2054 at 18. Most medical schools accept either; check, because a few do not.

courses.reason: Calculus I — 39 institutions, tied for the most widely carried course in the state. Required or strongly preferred by most medical schools, and a prerequisite for calculus-based physics.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Increasingly required outright, and you will read clinical trial evidence for forty years.
⚠ Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Not optional any more: the MCAT's psychological, social and biological foundations of behavior section is a quarter of the examination.
⚠ General Sociology — 29 institutions. The other half of that MCAT section, and the one pre-medical students most often skip and then regret.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Universally required, and the personal statement and secondary essays are a real part of the application.
English Composition II — 37 institutions. The second composition requirement most medical schools name explicitly.
Human Nutrition — 13 institutions. Not required, named because it is the cheapest useful preparation for the chronic-disease management that dominates actual practice.
Microbiology — 16 institutions. Not universally required but widely recommended, and directly useful for the infectious disease content of both the MCAT and the first two years.
